pack: Ledger History and State-Sync in postfiatd

rules.statement: One InboundLedger acquire cycle uses a 3000 ms timeout (ledgerAcquireTimeout).
rules.title: Each ledger acquire times out after 3000 ms

rules.statement: onTimer marks the acquire failed once timeouts_ exceeds ledgerTimeoutRetriesMax (6).
rules.title: More than 6 timeouts fails the acquire

rules.statement: After the first timeout queries switch to qtINDIRECT; after ledgerBecomeAggressiveThreshold (4) timeouts with no progress, the acquire asks peers directly by hash for the exact missing nodes.
rules.title: After 4 timeouts the acquire goes aggressive and indirect

rules.statement: An acquire starts with 5 peers and adds 3 per timeout; each pass asks for at most 256 missing nodes, 128 nodes per reply, 12 nodes blindly.
rules.title: Peer and node request counts are fixed constants

rules.statement: When a fetched header's hash differs from the requested hash, or its sequence differs from the requested sequence, the ledger is marked failed with the note that it can never be acquired.
rules.title: A header whose hash or sequence mismatches can never be acquired

rules.statement: tryDB fails the acquire when the ledger header carries a zero account hash.
rules.title: A ledger with a zero account hash fails acquisition

rules.statement: complete_ is set only when mHaveHeader, mHaveState, and mHaveTransactions are all true; a zero transaction hash counts as having no transactions to fetch.
rules.title: An acquire completes only with header, state, and transactions

rules.statement: Recent failures are kept for kReacquireInterval (5 minutes); isFailure expires them after that interval, so the same ledger is not retried sooner.
rules.title: A failed acquire blocks reacquisition for 5 minutes

rules.statement: acquire returns empty when isNeedNetworkLedger() is true, unless the reason is GENERIC or CONSENSUS; history fetches wait until the node has a network ledger.
rules.title: Acquires are refused while the node still needs a network ledger

rules.statement: LedgerMaster keeps fetch packs in a TaggedCache named FetchPack with capacity 65536 and a 45-second lifetime.
rules.title: The fetch-pack cache holds 65536 entries for 45 seconds

rules.statement: getFetchPack returns data only when sha512Half of the data equals the requested hash; the entry is deleted from the cache whether or not the check passes.
rules.title: A fetch-pack entry is verified by hash and consumed on read

rules.statement: makeFetchPack returns immediately when the request uptime is more than 1 second old.
rules.title: A fetch-pack request older than 1 second is dropped as stale

source.anchor: Too busy to make fetch pack

rules.statement: makeFetchPack returns without replying when the fee tracker reports the node loaded locally, or when the validated ledger age exceeds 40 seconds.
rules.title: A loaded node, or one whose validated ledger is older than 40 s, refuses to build a fetch pack

rules.statement: Building a fetch pack walks backwards from the requested ledger adding headers, up to 16384 account-state nodes and 512 transaction nodes per ledger, and stops at 512 objects or when 1 second has elapsed.
rules.title: A fetch pack is capped at 512 objects, 16384 state nodes, 512 transaction nodes, 1 second

source.anchor: Peer requests fetch pack for ledger we don't have

rules.statement: makeFetchPack charges the requesting peer (feeRequestNoReply or feeMalformedRequest) when the have-ledger is absent, open, below getEarliestFetch, or its parent is absent.
rules.title: Fetch-pack requests for a missing, open, too-early, or parentless ledger are refused and the peer charged

rules.statement: getFetchPack picks, among active peers whose range covers [missing, missing+1], the peer with the highest latency-biased score, and sends it an otFETCH_PACK request for the hash of ledger missing+1.
rules.title: A fetch pack is requested from the highest-scoring peer that holds the range

rules.statement: gotStaleData re-serializes wire-format nodes with their prefix and stores them via addFetchPack, so data paid for is kept in case it is needed later.
rules.title: Stale ledger data received for a finished acquire is stashed in the fetch-pack cache

rules.statement: doAdvance fetches history only when there is nothing to publish, the node is not loaded, fewer than 10 jtPUBOLDLEDGER jobs are queued, valid and published sequences match, validated age is under 1 minute, and write load is under 8192.
rules.title: History backfill runs only while the node is in sync

rules.statement: MAX_LEDGER_GAP is 100: the node does not catch up more than 100 ledgers in one step (and the comment notes it cannot exceed 256).
rules.title: Catch-up is capped at a 100-ledger gap

rules.statement: A missing ledger is acquired when it is at or after the current ledger, within ledgerHistory of the current ledger, or at or after the SHAMapStore minimum online ledger.
rules.title: shouldAcquire fetches only current, in-window, or minimum-online ledgers

rules.statement: Config LEDGER_HISTORY defaults to 256 and FETCH_DEPTH to 1000000000.
rules.title: Ledger history defaults to 256 ledgers; fetch depth defaults to 1,000,000,000

rules.statement: isCaughtUp returns false when the published ledger age exceeds 3 minutes, when either close time is zero, or when the validated close is more than 90 seconds after the published close.
rules.title: Caught-up means a fresh published ledger and a validated ledger within 90 seconds of it

rules.statement: getValidatedLedgerAge returns two weeks when no validated ledger close time has been recorded.
rules.title: With no validated ledger, the validated age is two weeks

rules.statement: fetchForHistory acquires by hash; when the acquire returns nothing and the sequence is above the earliest ledger, it requests a fetch pack only if fetch_seq_ is not already that sequence, then records it.
rules.title: A failed history acquire requests a fetch pack at most once per missing sequence

rules.statement: When a history ledger is not acquired, the node prefetches up to min(ledger_fetch_size_, missing - earliestLedgerSeq + 1) ledgers below it, and never below the earliest ledger sequence.
rules.title: Prefetch below a missing ledger is bounded by the fetch size and the earliest ledger

rules.statement: setFullLedger compares the previous ledger's hash with the new ledger's parentHash; on a hash mismatch or a missing previous ledger it calls fixMismatch, which walks backwards invalidating ledgers until the chain closes.
rules.title: Accepting a ledger re-checks its parent; a mismatch invalidates the previous ledger

rules.statement: insert raises on a mutable ledger and asserts a nonzero state-map hash before caching the ledger by hash and, when validated, by sequence.
rules.title: LedgerHistory accepts only immutable ledgers with a nonzero state hash

rules.statement: When a sequence is not in the validated index, getLedgerBySeq loads it from the database by index, asserts the loaded ledger's sequence equals the requested one, and returns null otherwise.
rules.title: getLedgerBySeq falls back to the database and requires the sequence to match

rules.statement: Whether the ledger comes from the cache or the database, getLedgerByHash asserts immutability and that info().hash equals the requested hash.
rules.title: getLedgerByHash asserts the returned ledger's hash equals the requested hash

rules.statement: A parent-hash disagreement is logged as a sync issue, a close-time disagreement as Byzantine failure, and a consensus-hash disagreement as a transaction-set difference; equal transaction sets are also logged explicitly.
rules.title: handleMismatch classifies built-vs-validated disagreements

rules.statement: validatedLedger compares a previously built hash with the newly validated hash and calls handleMismatch when they differ, instead of silently replacing the entry.
rules.title: Building then validating the same sequence with different hashes triggers mismatch analysis

rules.statement: LedgerHistory keeps the consensus-validated map in a TaggedCache of 64 entries with a 5-minute lifetime.
rules.title: The consensus-validated cache holds 64 entries for 5 minutes

source.anchor: number of async reads per pass

rules.statement: getMissingNodes asserts a nonzero root and max > 0, reads up to 512 nodes asynchronously per pass, and starts traversal at a randomly chosen first child so parallel threads request different sets.
rules.title: SHAMap sync walks missing nodes with 512 async reads per pass and a random start

rules.statement: AccountStateSF::getNode and TransactionStateSF::getNode both return the fetch-pack entry for a node hash when the node is not in the local store.
rules.title: SHAMap sync filters fall back to the fetch-pack cache for missing nodes

rules.statement: neededHashes returns the root hash when the map hash is zero, otherwise the missing nodes up to the requested maximum, filtered by the SHAMap sync filter.
rules.title: neededHashes returns the root first, then the missing nodes

rules.statement: trigger sets querydepth 0 for blind queries, 1 when replying to a peer, and 2 when the peer is high-latency.
rules.title: Query depth is 0 blind, 1 on reply, 2 for high-latency peers

rules.statement: Config LEDGER_REPLAY defaults to false; the experimental replay feature must be enabled explicitly.
rules.title: Ledger replay is disabled by default

rules.statement: LedgerReplayParameters caps replay at MAX_TASKS 10, MAX_TASK_SIZE 256 ledgers per task, MAX_QUEUED_TASKS 100; a task times out after 500 ms with at most max(10, ledgers x 2) timeouts, subtasks after 250 ms with at most 10 timeouts, falling back to a 1000 ms subtask timeout after 2 peers without the feature.
rules.title: Replay tasks are bounded: 10 tasks, 256 ledgers each, 500 ms timeouts

external.note: Matches code default LEDGER_HISTORY = 256 (Config.h:224); the docs figure is a deployment statement, not a code fact.
external.quote: An XRP Ledger server does not need to store more than the most recent 256 ledger versions to follow the consensus process and report the complete state of the ledger

rules.statement: The capacity-planning documentation states a server does not need to store more than the most recent 256 ledger versions to follow the consensus process and report the complete state.
rules.title: Docs: a server needs only the most recent 256 ledgers to follow consensus

external.note: Matches the code order: header first (InboundLedger trigger), state before transactions (comment at InboundLedger.cpp:619).
external.quote: Data arrives in the following order: 1. The hash of the ledger header 2. The ledger header 3. The root nodes of the transaction tree and state tree 4. The lower (non-root) nodes of the state tree 5. The lower (non-root) nodes of the transaction tree

rules.statement: The ledger directory reference describes peer delivery order: the hash of the ledger header, the ledger header, the transaction-tree and state-tree roots, the lower state-tree nodes, then the lower transaction-tree nodes.
rules.title: Docs: ledger data arrives header hash, header, roots, state nodes, transaction nodes

external.note: Matches the doAdvance sync gates (LedgerMaster.cpp:1948-1955) and the tryDB-then-peers order in InboundLedger.cpp:240-300.
external.quote: The server prioritizes keeping up with current ledgers. But if it is caught up on the current ledger, and there are no higher priority demands on the server, then it will attempt to back fill its historical ledgers. It fills in the historical ledger data first by attempting to retrieve it from the local database. If the local database does not have all of the necessary data then the server requests the remaining information from network peers.

rules.statement: The ledger directory reference states the server prioritizes keeping up with current ledgers and backfills history only when caught up, first from the local database and then from network peers.
rules.title: Docs: backfill happens only when caught up, local store first, then peers

external.note: Deployment guidance only; the code default for FETCH_DEPTH is 1000000000 (Config.h:225) and the clamp lives in SHAMapStore::clampFetchDepth.
external.quote: online_delete must not be greater than the [ledger_history] parameter. [fetch_depth] will be silently set to equal the online_delete setting if online_delete is greater than fetch_depth.

rules.statement: The storage documentation states online_delete must not be greater than the ledger_history parameter, and fetch_depth is silently set to equal online_delete when online_delete is greater than fetch_depth.
rules.title: Docs: online_delete is at least 256 and fetch_depth follows it when larger

model.note: The cap is code; the rounds figure is a model output, not a measured live value.

rules.statement: Applying the MAX_LEDGER_GAP cap of 100 per step, a gap of G ledgers needs at least ceil(G / 100) doAdvance rounds when peers cooperate and no round fails.
rules.title: Model: a gap of G ledgers needs ceil(G / 100) advance rounds to close

model.note: The check is code; the staged detection order in the simulator is a model.
model.parameter: sha512Half check (LedgerMaster.cpp:2043); SHAMap root verification in InboundLedger trigger

rules.statement: In the model, a node whose bytes do not hash to its advertised hash is rejected when the SHAMap root is verified or when getFetchPack compares sha512Half(data) with the requested hash; receipt alone never accepts data.
rules.title: Model: a tampered fetch-pack node is detected at the hash check, not at receipt

rules.note: No live node was run for this pack.
rules.statement: Whether real peers serve fetch packs, how many peers a node actually reaches, and how an eclipse or poisoning attempt plays out on the live network cannot be determined from the pinned source; only the local gates and checks are verifiable.
rules.title: Live peer behaviour under eclipse, churn, or targeted poisoning cannot be tested from source alone
